overview: USGS identifies the Bachelor Consolidated Mine and the lower Bachelor (Syracuse) tunnel as related workings; federal DMEA records later evaluated Bachelor Mine for lead-zinc, silver, gold, and copper.

timeline.text: Published origin dates conflict (1884, 1888, early 1890s); no exact discovery year is adopted.

moreHistory: The operator’s documented history identifies Charlie Armstrong, George Hurlburt, and J.
Frank Sanders as early owners; ore moved down Red Canyon to Bachelor Switch, while the associated Ash camp of about 200 included a mill, school, post office, and band.
In the 1920s Syracuse, New York investors financed the lower Syracuse Level, which became a major producing working and is the tunnel used by the modern mine tour.

Component safeguard: keep the original upper Bachelor main workings/portal, Ash camp and mill, Bachelor Switch, lower Syracuse Tunnel/current tour entrance, and later surface visitor facilities as separate linked components.
